subject: Dedicated capacity guidance — MVP tranche SKU allocation and ops runbook
messages:
From: Sophie Barnes <sophie@heliosai.com>

Cc: HeliosAI Procurement <procurement@heliosai.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing for Dedicated: long-context + bursty throughput

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the initial call this morning. To give you context for the sizing ask: HeliosAI is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production rollout. Our projected steady-state volume is modest (~250k tokens/day) but with a very skewed profile:~
- ~20% long-context requests (models with 32k+ contexts, KV-cache heavy, stateful sessions)
- ~70% mid/short generation (under 2k tokens, latency sensitive, high QPS bursts)
- ~10% embeddings & lower-cost search workloads

We're focused on predictable latency for short requests (95th < 250ms) and bounded tail for long-context work (<1s preferred), and we need a pricing window to provision reserved capacity (12-month) plus clear burst/fallback guidance.

Questions:
1) For a reserved commit, should we recommend a homogeneous pool (A100) or a mixed pool (H100 for long-context, A100 for throughput, L4 for embeddings/dev)?
2) Propose a sizing and reserve-to-burst strategy including headroom and expected cost delta.
3) Any operational caveats (tiling, KV cache memory, model quantization) to call out for procurement or infra?

Could you send a short tranche-level recommendation and ops runbook we can share with procurement? We need this by EOD Tuesday to keep internal timelines.

Best,
Sophie

Head of Platform, HeliosAI

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing for Dedicated: long-context + bursty throughput

Thanks Sophie — summary below and an initial tranche plan attached. Quick TL;DR: mixed reserved pool + burstable L4s for cost efficiency; pilot split to validate real-world token shapes before final commit.

Recommendation (MVP tranche) — reserve + burst mix
- Reserved (baseline) composition: 60% A100, 25% H100, 15% L4 (by reserved vGPU slot equivalence). Reasoning: A100 is the best cost/throughput for the high-QPS short-generation mix; H100 is needed for the 32k+ KV cache stability and model variants that degrade on smaller GPU memory; L4 reserved slice covers embeddings and dev traffic without incurring H100/A100 cost.
- Burst strategy: allow additional ephemeral L4s for 2x QPS spikes and a small (10%) autoscale buffer of A100s to absorb sustained bursts — H100 bursting is expensive, only used when long-context concurrency exceeds reserved headroom.
- Headroom sizing: target 40–50% concurrency headroom on reserved pools to keep 95th latency SLOs; rely on prefix/KV caching to shave token cost for long-context sessions.

Operational notes
- Tiling & slotting: long-context models benefit from slot consolidation (fewer slots with bigger memory) to avoid OOM; recommend pinning 32k models to H100s with dedicated KV cache reservation.
- Quantization/variants: prepare int8-int4 quantized variants for A100 & L4 where possible to reduce memory pressure; keep a higher-precision H100 variant for quality-sensitive long-contexts.
- Fallbacks: automatic model downgrade policy (H100 -> A100 quantized -> L4 quantized) with quality gate can preserve availability during capacity stress.

Cost delta (rough)
- Baseline (12-month reserved): mix above estimates ~ +18–25% vs homogeneous A100 reserve because H100 unit cost is higher; but expected to reduce burst cost by ~35% because H100s reduce need for excessive A100 reserve to satisfy long-context requests.

Next steps / deliverables (action items)
1) Iren e & Jordan: run capacity simulation using Sophie's usage_snapshot and our tile sizing tool (see attached capacity_sim_input.csv). Deliver by EOD Tuesday.
2) Mina: draft ops runbook with KV pinning, autoscale thresholds, and fallback policies — attach as MVP_tranche_ops_runbook.pdf.
3) Aditya (me): produce tranche-level pricing and HubSpot entry with DocuSign timeline 

Attached: capacity_sim_input.csv, MVP_tranche_ops_runbook.pdf

Let me know if you want an alternate split (e.g., memory-first 40/40/20).

— Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Sophie — attached is the one-page MAP and a short fallback appendix. Key deliverables and timeline below so procurement has something executable: 

Week 0 (today — Tue): intake + baseline sim inputs captured (capacity_sim_input.csv).
Week 1: Redwood runs capacity simulations (Irene & Jordan) and returns recommended reserved slot counts per SKU + autoscale thresholds.
Week 2: Pilot: spin dedicated pilot pool (limited commit) for 7 days; run synthetic plus 20% mirrored production traffic. Evaluate latency and quality metrics.
Week 3: Procurement review + contract redlines; finalize reserve counts and discount tiers.
Week 4: Commit + gradual rollout; Redwood to provide onboarding runbook and KMS integration steps.

Fallback appendix (brief) — expected quality delta
- H100 high-precision variant: baseline quality (100) for long-context tasks.
- A100 quantized variant (int8): ~3–6% drop on long-context token-likelihood metrics, but latency is often similar on mid-length prompts; good for mixed load.
- L4 quantized variant (int4 or int8 depending on model): larger delta (~8–12%) on very long-context tasks; acceptable for embeddings & lower-cost search.

SOC2 / KMS
- Public evidence & architecture: https://redwood.com/compliance/soc2 (read-only links included in the MAP). Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) for private deployments; Redwood Private includes HSM options on request.

Attachments included: MAP_helios_mvp_tranche.pdf, capacity_sim_input.csv, MVP_tranche_ops_runbook.pdf
